title: Orchestrate dashboard request intake and enterprise data-contracts for console reporting
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and platform teams are submitting ad-hoc requests for console dashboards, CSV/streaming exports, and cost-breakdown reports with inconsistent signal (incomplete requirements, missing SLAs, unclear data contracts). This causes long discovery loops, rework between Data/Backend/Console teams, and unpredictable delivery timelines.

Goal: Create an orchestration and triage playbook for enterprise reporting requests that (1) standardizes intake fields, (2) defines a priority rubric tied to business outcomes and engineering cost, (3) creates a minimal data-contract template for exports/dashboards, and (4) establishes SLA/response expectations for customers and internal stakeholders. This ticket scopes the PM work to author the playbook, run two pilot triages with sales/customer success, and produce a companion Confluence template and a short developer onboarding checklist.
acceptance_criteria: An intake form template (Confluence + Support intake) that captures required fields: business use-case, expected frequency/volume, primary KPIs, data retention needs, PII classification, export format, and requester SLAs.
A written prioritization rubric that maps request attributes to priority buckets (P0/P1/P2) with rationale and estimated engineering effort ranges.
A one-page data-contract template for exports/dashboards listing required fields, schema expectations, freshness SLA, and transformation notes.
Two pilot triage sessions completed with Sales/CS and two customer requests processed using the new rubric; outcomes logged and lessons captured.
A short README in the Console team's handbook with onboarding steps and links to the template and sample GitHub issues/prioritization records.
updates: 2025-02-25: Ticket created after backlog refinement with Growth and Enterprise CS. Key drivers: recurring ad-hoc export requests from 3 enterprise accounts and recent support escalations about inconsistent billing breakdowns.

2025-02-27: Scoping call with Console Eng (lead: Priya Rao) and Data Platform (lead: Tomas Alvarez). Agreed minimum required fields for intake and a lightweight data-contract; engineering prefers schema-first CSV with column-level types.
2025-02-28: Draft prioritization rubric shared with Head of Sales and Solutions Engineering for feedback. Sales requested explicit weighting for revenue-impact and required time-to-value.

2025-03-01: Incorporating feedback from legal on PII and retention; added mandatory PII classification field in intake and flagging mechanism for security_review_required. Preparing two pilot requests for 2025-03-03 triage session.
decisions: Keep intake as two-tier: a short public-facing request form for customers and an internal expanded intake for engineering review. This reduces friction while capturing necessary engineering details.
Prioritization rubric will combine customer revenue impact, product risk (privacy/security), implementation cost (estimated points), and frequency/scale. Each dimension is scored 1-5 and summed.
For exports, the data-contract will be prescriptive (column names, types, cardinality expectations) and required before engineering work begins. Exceptions require Solutions Eng sign-off.

SLA expectations: initial acknowledgement within 3 business days; triage decision and priority assignment within 10 business days for enterprise customers. Implementation timelines will be estimated post-triage.
next_steps: Finalize Confluence draft and publish as 'reporting-intake-template-v0.1' by 2025-03-04.
Run two pilot triage sessions (2025-03-03 and 2025-03-06) with Sales/CS and log results under the ticket; iterate on rubric scoring thresholds.
Create a sample GitHub issue/epic template for engineering with required checklist fields linked to the data-contract and attach to Console repo.
Schedule a 30-minute working session with Legal and Security to formalize the PII handling flow and approval gates for exports (target 2025-03-10).
